title: Toby, Johnny Hodges and Barney Bigard
summary: Cootie got along with Hodges, called Bigard a different type but friendly; the band was like a family.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: He was from Washington. I forget his name. There was some brothers.
Yeah. What were you fixing to say?
I was fixing to say then Toby was in the band.
You hit it off good with Toby, didn't you?
He was always a lighthearted guy, wasn't he?
Johnny was always quiet, wasn't he?
Yeah. Me and Johnny. Me and Johnny was good friends. We was good pals.
Oh, that's good. That's what -- you mean always, right from the start.
That's very good. What about Buster? I don't mean Buster. I mean Barney.
Oh, Barney's not as easy to get along with, is he?
He's all right, you know. But he was a different type of fellow.
I don't know. Barney, he was just sort of a peculiar type. You know. He -- it's kind of hard to say.
No. I don't know how to describe it.
Describe Barney. I tell you. But we all got along fine.
Well, I mean, it was like a family, with everybody having their own different ways of being, and then everybody understands how each person is.
